s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss with intraocular hemorrhage and crystalline deposits
salient_findings: Spontaneous hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage in one eye
Presence of glistening crystals in the anterior chamber
Iridescent, needle-like crystals floating in the aqueous
key_facts: Patient is a young girl
Right eye is blind
Hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage occurred spontaneously
Multiple glistening crystals were observed in the anterior chamber
Number of aqueous crystals increased as hyphema resolved
Iridescent, needle-like crystals are floating freely in the aqueous
Morning glory optic disc anomaly is present
Low-lying detachment of the peripapillary retina is observed
Chronic retinal detachment is present after vitreous hemorrhage resolution

shortlist.label: Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of iridescent, needle-like crystals in the aqueous humor

shortlist.label: Cystinosis
shortlist.why_kept: Ocular crystals and potential for vision loss

shortlist.label: Primary hyperoxaluria type 1
shortlist.why_kept: Association with oxalate crystals in the eye

shortlist.label: Morning glory syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of morning glory optic disc anomaly and retinal detachment

shortlist.label: Sjögren-Larsson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Association with crystalline deposits in the eye

raw.rationale: The presence of a morning glory optic disc anomaly, low-lying detachment of the peripapillary retina, and chronic retinal detachment are characteristic features of Morning glory syndrome, which can also explain the spontaneous hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage.

rejected.label: Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy
rejected.why: While it involves crystals, it primarily affects the cornea and retina, not typically associated with morning glory disc anomaly

rejected.label: Cystinosis
rejected.why: Involves cystine crystals in the eye, but typically presents with systemic symptoms and does not explain the morning glory disc anomaly

rejected.label: Primary hyperoxaluria type 1
rejected.why: Involves oxalate crystals, but is a systemic disease with primary renal manifestations, not directly related to morning glory disc anomaly

rejected.label: Sjögren-Larsson syndrome
rejected.why: Involves retinal changes, but is characterized by systemic symptoms like ichthyosis and spasticity, not specifically related to morning glory disc anomaly
